newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha lower as Asian prices drop.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha lower as Asian prices drop.

text.p: NWE naphtha fell on Monday as crude losses late on Friday along with a collapse in all-important Asian prices took their toll, traders said.
Swaps were talked around the $184.50/$185.50 cif NWE for April level in later trade, having falled into the low $180s in early trade. May was seen as $1 above April.
Traders attributed the initial falls to crude losses on Friday - May IPE Brent sank as low as $17.65 a barrel in the final hour of the session.
Its modest recovery as Monday progressed was seen as the reason for naphtha's slight improvement.
But prices remained very much under pressure as NWE traders anxiously monitored the situation in Asia.
Naphtha prices fell to a six-month low in Japan and a five-month low in Singapore due to softer crude and weak demand in Asia.
Naphtha swaps shed 70 cents per barrel against Friday to $21.50/$21.70 while Japan's open-spec first-half June dropped $5 per tonne to $208/$209.
Traders said that most end-users in Northwestern Europe appeared to be well covered.
